facts.text: In a hypothetical run, context length 2048 uses 7 GB and 8192 uses 11 GB.
Model, runtime and hardware are held fixed.
No output quality or throughput results were collected.

draft.title: Hypothetical Memory Usage: Context Length vs. RAM in Local LLMs
draft.body: This post explores a hypothetical scenario investigating the relationship between context length and RAM consumption for local large language models. In this *hypothetical* setup, with the model, runtime, and hardware kept constant (F2), we observed distinct RAM footprints. A context length of 2048 tokens was associated with approximately 7 GB of RAM usage, while increasing the context length to 8192 tokens hypothetically required around 11 GB of RAM (F1). It's crucial to note that this experiment was purely hypothetical; no actual measurements were taken, and no results regarding output quality or processing speed were recorded (F3). The objective was solely to illustrate the potential memory scaling with context length. Further investigation would be needed to confirm these hypothetical figures and explore their impact on practical usability.
draft.plan: Discuss the hypothetical RAM usage increase with context length. Explicitly state the hypothetical nature of the findings and the lack of quality/throughput data. Invite discussion on expected RAM scaling in local LLMs.
